FOUNDING CHARTER · QUANTITATIVE SECTOR ARCHITECTURE

Why quiet two-pillar discipline outlasts loud stock picking.

Most households approaching or living in retirement do not lose sleep—or hard-earned capital—because they ignored the market. They lose both because financial media pushes investors to chase dozens of noisy stock tips at once, quietly drifting into pure technology concentration right before a multi-year downturn.

We built Truth of Market for a calmer purpose. Rather than sending speculative trade alerts, our quantitative research desk focuses on one enduring discipline: participating in structural semiconductor innovation (SMH) while anchoring household composure with non-cyclical healthcare cash flows (XLV) and short-term US Treasury reserves (SGOV).

Through a brief four-question assessment below, this platform maps your initial sector baseline, tracks daily public market temperature so you know when historical risk has stretched to extremes, and provides structured retirement withdrawal and tax-account planning tools.

COMPLIMENTARY EXECUTION REFERENCE ($0)

US Brokerage Limit-Order & ETF Reference

I. Place Limit Orders Rather Than Market Orders
On Fidelity, Charles Schwab, or Vanguard, select Limit Order rather than Market Order during the first 15 minutes after the 9:30 AM ET open to avoid temporary bid-ask spread widening on ETFs.
II. Non-Leveraged 1x Spot Sector ETFs Only
Both SMH (Semiconductors) and XLV (US Healthcare) are unleveraged 1x spot ETFs free from daily 3x leveraged volatility-reset decay.
III. Short-Term US Treasury Liquidity Cushion
Near-term household cash reserves can be insulated in 0–3 month US Treasury bills (SGOV) or government money-market funds (SPAXX / SWVXX / VMFXX).
